title: Online co-op is now in the Portal Beasts demo! Here’s what I’ve been building with AI
author: PortalBeasts
selftext:
Hey everyone! I’m working on **Portal Beasts**, a creature-collecting RPG where you explore different worlds, catch beasts, build your team, and fight alongside them in real-time combat.

I’ve now added **two-player online co-op**, with its own campaign. You can explore together, battle wild beasts, and build your own teams. The video shows some of it in action!

Since this is an AI game dev community, here’s where AI fits into my workflow:

* **Coding and debugging:** AI helps me implement features, investigate bugs, and build tests.
* **Pixel art:** I use PixelLab for parts of the creature and environment artwork, including directional sprites and animations.
* **Iteration:** There’s a lot of checking and correcting results—keeping a creature’s design consistent across eight directions has been a challenge of its own!

The game is built in **Godot**, with Aseprite also used in the art workflow.

**Co-op is still in beta, so expect bugs and rough edges.** I’ve been testing with different PCs and connections, but connection stability, combat synchronization, and performance still need more real-world testing.

The demo is available on Steam. If you try it with a friend, I’d love to hear what felt fun, what was confusing, and what broke. Reports from the joining player are especially helpful.

Happy to answer questions about the game or the AI workflow!  
  
**Try the free demo on Steam:** [https://store.steampowered.com/app/4545580/Portal\_Beasts\_Demo/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4545580/Portal_Beasts_Demo/)
